questions.question_text: The distance between P(0,b) and Q(a,0) is:
questions.explanation: Distance formula gives √((a−0)²+(0−b)²)=√(a²+b²).
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 13; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: P divides the segment joining A(5,−2) and B(9,6) internally in the ratio 3:1. Find P.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 15; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: P(1,10/3) divides the segment joining A(−3,2) and B(3,4). In what ratio AP:PB does it divide it?
questions.explanation: Using the x-coordinate section formula, 1=(3m−3n)/(m+n), so m=2n. The y-coordinate then is (4m+2n)/(m+n)=10/3, confirming AP:PB=2:1.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 17; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the coordinates of the point that divides the segment joining (2,4) and (6,8) externally in the ratio 5:3.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 18; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the ratio in which the segment joining A(3,−5) and B(5,4) is divided by the x-axis.
questions.explanation: At the x-axis y=0. For AP:PB=m:n, (4m−5n)/(m+n)=0, hence m:n=5:4.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 19; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the slope of the line through P(−4,7) and Q(2,3).
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 21; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: What angle does the line through (√3,1) and (√15,√5) make with the positive x-axis?
questions.explanation: Its slope is (√5−1)/(√15−√3)=1/√3, so the inclination θ satisfies tanθ=1/√3 and θ=30°.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry  01_.pdf, PDF page 22; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the reflection of (7,4) in the point (1,3).
questions.explanation: The reflection point is the opposite endpoint of a segment whose midpoint is (1,3): (x,y)=(2·1−7,2·3−4)=(−5,2).
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 23; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the perpendicular distance from (−3,4) to the line 3x+4y−5=0.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 13; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,4), (−4,3), and (8,6).
questions.explanation: Shoelace gives half of |3(3−6)+(−4)(6−4)+8(4−3)|=|-9-8+8|/2=9/2 square units.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 14; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: Find the area of the quadrilateral with consecutive vertices (−4,5), (0,7), (5,−5), and (−4,−2).
questions.explanation: Shoelace: absolute difference of diagonal sums is 121; area=121/2 square units.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 15; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: For what value of k do the lines 5x+20y=11 and 2x+ky=17 intersect?
questions.explanation: They are parallel when determinant 5k−40=0, i.e. k=8. They intersect for every other real k.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 16; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: For what value of k do x+3y+7=0 and 4x+ky+19=0 have no solution?
questions.explanation: No solution requires equal x/y coefficient ratios but unequal constant ratios: 1/4=3/k gives k=12; 7/19≠1/4.
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 17; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: A line ax+by=c, where a,b,c>0, meets the coordinate axes at P and Q. Find the area of triangle OPQ.
questions.explanation: The intercepts are c/a and c/b, so the right-triangle area is (1/2)(c/a)(c/b)=c²/(2ab).
questions.source: Coordinate Geometry 02_.pdf, PDF page 19; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: In which quadrant does (−4,7) lie?
questions.explanation: x<0 and y>0 identify Quadrant II.

questions.question_text: Which point lies on the y-axis?
questions.explanation: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0.

questions.question_text: Find the distance between (1,2) and (4,6).
Find the midpoint of (−2,5) and (6,1).
questions.explanation: Average corresponding coordinates: ((−2+6)/2,(5+1)/2)=(2,3).

questions.question_text: Reflect (3,−8) across the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Reflection across the x-axis preserves x and changes the sign of y.

questions.question_text: Reflect (−6,2) in the origin.
questions.explanation: Origin reflection maps (x,y) to (−x,−y).

questions.question_text: What is the slope of the line through (−1,4) and (3,4)?
questions.explanation: The y-coordinates are equal, so the line is horizontal and its slope is 0.

questions.question_text: What is the slope of the vertical line through (5,−2) and (5,9)?
questions.explanation: The slope denominator Δx is zero for a vertical line.

questions.question_text: What is the y-coordinate of every point on the x-axis?
questions.explanation: The x-axis is defined by y=0.

questions.question_text: A point has x<0 and y<0. In which quadrant is it?
questions.explanation: Both coordinates negative define Quadrant III.

questions.question_text: Translate (2,−3) by the vector (−4,5).
questions.explanation: Add vector components: (2−4,−3+5)=(−2,2).

questions.question_text: What is the absolute value of the abscissa of (−7,0)?
questions.explanation: The abscissa is the first coordinate, −7; its absolute value is 7.

questions.question_text: In the point (−4,−6), what is the ordinate?
questions.explanation: The ordinate is the second coordinate, which is −6.

questions.question_text: Which pair of points lies on the same horizontal line?
questions.explanation: Points on the same horizontal line have equal y-coordinates; only this pair has matching second coordinates.

questions.question_text: The midpoint of A(1,−2) and B(x,6) is (4,2). Find x.
questions.explanation: The midpoint x-coordinate gives (1+x)/2=4, hence x=7; the y-coordinate also averages to 2.

questions.question_text: Which quadrant contains (5,−1)?
questions.explanation: Positive x and negative y define Quadrant IV.

questions.question_text: Find the distance from (−3,4) to the origin.
questions.explanation: Distance from origin is √(x²+y²)=√(9+16)=5.

questions.question_text: A point is 4 units left and 3 units above the origin. What are its coordinates?
questions.explanation: Left means negative x and above means positive y.

questions.question_text: If P=(a,b), what are the coordinates of its reflection in the y-axis?
questions.explanation: Reflection across the y-axis reverses x and preserves y.

questions.question_text: Find the slope of the line through (2,−1) and (6,7).
A line has slope 3 and passes through (0,−2). What is its y-intercept?
questions.explanation: At x=0 the point on the line is (0,−2), so the y-intercept is −2.

questions.question_text: Which ordered pair satisfies y=2x+1?
questions.explanation: Substitution gives 5=2·2+1; the other listed pairs fail the equation.

questions.question_text: How many units apart are the parallel lines x=−2 and x=5?
questions.explanation: Their horizontal separation is |5−(−2)|=7.

questions.question_text: The point (x,−4) lies on the y-axis. Find x.
questions.explanation: Points on the y-axis have x-coordinate zero.

questions.question_text: What is the reflection of (−2,−7) across the x-axis?
questions.explanation: An x-axis reflection preserves the abscissa and negates the ordinate.

questions.question_text: Find the centroid of the triangle with vertices (0,0), (6,0), and (0,9).
questions.explanation: The centroid averages vertex coordinates: ((0+6+0)/3,(0+0+9)/3)=(2,3).

questions.question_text: A point on the x-axis is 6 units from the origin and lies to the left. Find it.
questions.explanation: On x-axis y=0; left of origin means x=−6.

questions.question_text: For what value of t is (t,2) in Quadrant I?
questions.explanation: Quadrant I requires both coordinates positive; y=2 is positive and so t must be positive.

questions.question_text: Which non-origin point is equidistant from the x- and y-axes?
questions.explanation: Distances to the axes are |y| and |x|; here both are 4. The origin is excluded by the stem.

questions.question_text: Find the point that divides (−4,3) and (8,−5) internally in the ratio 1:2.
The midpoint of A(−3,5) and B(x,y) is (2,−1). Find B.
Find the ratio in which P(2,1) divides the segment joining A(−1,−2) and B(5,4).
questions.explanation: P is the midpoint: coordinates average to ((−1+5)/2,(−2+4)/2)=(2,1), so the ratio is 1:1.

questions.question_text: A point divides A(1,−3) and B(7,9) in ratio 2:1 internally. Find its y-coordinate.
Find the slope of the line through (−2,5) and (4,−7).
A line through (3,−2) is parallel to the line through (−1,4) and (2,10). Find its slope.
questions.explanation: The reference slope is (10−4)/(2−(−1))=6/3=2; parallel lines have equal slopes.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the line with slope −3 passing through (2,5).
questions.explanation: Point-slope form: y−5=−3(x−2), hence y=−3x+11.

questions.question_text: Find the x-intercept of 2x+3y=12.
questions.explanation: Set y=0, obtaining 2x=12 and x=6.

questions.question_text: Find the y-intercept of 5x−2y=8.
questions.explanation: Set x=0; −2y=8, so y=−4.

questions.question_text: Are (1,2), (3,6), and (5,10) collinear?
questions.explanation: Each point satisfies y=2x, so all three lie on the same line.

questions.question_text: Find the intersection point of x+y=7 and x−y=1.
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x=8, so x=4; then y=3.

questions.question_text: The distance between (x,1) and (2,5) is 5. If x>2, find x.
questions.explanation: (x−2)²+16=25 gives (x−2)²=9; x>2 selects x=5.

questions.question_text: Find the point where y=2x+1 meets the x-axis.
A line through (1,3) and (5,11) meets the y-axis at what value?
questions.explanation: Slope=2, so y−3=2(x−1), or y=2x+1; y-intercept=1.

questions.question_text: Find the distance from (−2,7) to the line y=3.
questions.explanation: The horizontal line has constant y=3; perpendicular distance is |7−3|=4.

questions.question_text: The midpoint of A and B is (3,−2). If A=(−1,4), find B.
questions.explanation: Coordinate sums must be twice the midpoint: B=(6−(−1),−4−4)=(7,−8).

questions.question_text: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to y=(1/4)x−6.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular nonvertical slopes multiply to −1; reciprocal of 1/4 with opposite sign is −4.

questions.question_text: For which value of k are (2,1), (5,7), and (8,k) collinear?
questions.explanation: First two give slope 6/3=2. From (5,7), moving to x=8 raises y by 2·3=6; k=13.

questions.question_text: A line has intercepts 4 on x-axis and 6 on y-axis. Find its equation in intercept form.
questions.explanation: Intercept form is x/a+y/b=1, with a=4 and b=6.

questions.question_text: A triangle has vertices (−2,0), (4,0), and (1,h). Its area is 12. If h>0, find h.
questions.explanation: The base length is 6; 6h/2=12 gives h=4.

questions.question_text: Find the point that divides (−3,2) and (9,8) externally in ratio 2:1.
A line passes through (−2,3) and is parallel to 4x−2y=7. Find its y-intercept.
questions.explanation: The given line has slope 2. Through (−2,3): y−3=2(x+2), so y=2x+7 and its y-intercept is 7.

questions.question_text: Three consecutive vertices of an axis-parallel rectangle are (−1,2), (5,2), and (5,−3). Find the fourth vertex.
questions.explanation: The first pair defines the top horizontal side and the second pair the right vertical side; the missing corner combines x=−1 with y=−3.

questions.question_text: A point (a,−6) is 10 units from (2,−6). Find the possible values of a.
questions.explanation: Equal y-coordinates make distance |a−2|=10, giving a=−8 or 12.

questions.question_text: Find k if the distance between (k,−4) and (3,8) is 13 and k<3.
questions.explanation: (k−3)²+12²=13² gives (k−3)²=25; k=−2 or 8, and k<3 selects −2.

questions.question_text: Find the circumcentre of the triangle with vertices (0,0), (6,0), and (0,8).
questions.explanation: The triangle is right-angled at the origin, so its circumcentre is the midpoint of its hypotenuse from (6,0) to (0,8): (3,4).

questions.question_text: Find the value of t for which (1,2), (4,6), and (t,10) are collinear.
questions.explanation: Slope between the first points is 4/3. Collinearity requires (10−6)/(t−4)=4/3, giving t=7.

questions.question_text: Find the perpendicular distance from (2,−1) to 6x−8y+3=0.
The lines 2x+y=10 and x−y=2 intersect at P. Find the distance from P to (1,−1).
questions.explanation: Solving gives P=(4,2). The distance to (1,−1) is √((4−1)²+(2+1)²)=√18=3√2.

questions.question_text: Two lines 3x+ky=5 and 6x+4y=9 are parallel and distinct. Find k.
questions.explanation: Parallelism requires 3/6=k/4=1/2, so k=2. Their constants are not in the same ratio (5/9≠1/2), so they are distinct.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the line through the intersection of x+y=5 and 2x−y=1, with slope 3.
questions.explanation: Solving gives intersection (2,3). Point-slope form y−3=3(x−2), hence y=3x−3.

questions.question_text: A triangle has vertices (0,0), (p,0), and (0,q), with area 30 and p:q=5:3. If p,q>0, find p+q.
questions.explanation: pq/2=30 gives pq=60. With p:q=5:3, let p=5u,q=3u;15u²=60 so u=2 and p+q=16.

questions.question_text: Find the point on the x-axis equidistant from A(−2,3) and B(4,3).
questions.explanation: Let P=(x,0). Equate squared distances: (x+2)²+9=(x−4)²+9; simplifying gives 12x=12, so x=1.

questions.question_text: A line cuts positive intercepts a and b and has equation x/a+y/b=1. If its intercept triangle has area 24 and a:b=3:4, find a+b.
questions.explanation: ab/2=24 gives ab=48. Set a=3u,b=4u;12u²=48 so u=2 and a+b=14.

questions.question_text: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (a,0), (0,b), and (−a,0), where a,b>0.
questions.explanation: The base on the x-axis has length 2a and height b; area=(2a·b)/2=ab.

questions.question_text: Find the value of m if the line through (−1,4) and (m,−2) is perpendicular to 2x+3y=7.
questions.explanation: The given line slope is −2/3, so a perpendicular line has slope 3/2. Thus (−2−4)/(m+1)=−6/(m+1)=3/2, giving m=−5.

questions.question_text: The points A(0,0), B(6,0), and C(3,k) form a right angle at C. If k>0, find k.
questions.explanation: At C, vectors CA=(−3,−k), CB=(3,−k). Perpendicularity gives CA·CB=−9+k²=0; k=3 since k>0.

questions.question_text: A line through (2,−3) has x-intercept 5. Find its slope.
questions.explanation: Slope between (2,−3) and (5,0) is (0+3)/(5−2)=1.

questions.question_text: A point P divides A(−4,1) and B(8,7) internally so that AP:PB=2:1. Find the distance OP.
Find the area of the quadrilateral with vertices (0,0), (6,0), (5,4), and (1,3) in this order.
questions.explanation: Shoelace diagonal sums differ by |39−4|=35; area=35/2.

questions.question_text: Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x−4y+8=0 and 6x−8y−5=0.
questions.explanation: Divide the second equation by 2: 3x−4y−5/2=0. Distance=|8−(−5/2)|/√(9+16)=21/10.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the line through (−2,5) and perpendicular to 3x−2y=8.
questions.explanation: Given slope is 3/2; perpendicular slope=−2/3. Through point: y−5=−2/3(x+2), which rearranges to 2x+3y−11=0.

questions.question_text: For what value of k are (k,1), (2,3), and (6,11) collinear?
questions.explanation: Slope from (2,3) to (6,11) is 2, so line is y=2x−1. Setting y=1 gives x=1.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining (−2,1) and (4,5).
questions.explanation: The midpoint is (1,3); segment slope is 2/3, so the perpendicular slope is −3/2. Through (1,3): y−3=−3(x−1)/2, or 3x+2y−9=0.

questions.question_text: A line through (1,−2) is perpendicular to the line joining (−3,4) and (5,0). Find its y-intercept.
questions.explanation: The joining line slope is (0−4)/(5+3)=−1/2; a perpendicular line has slope 2. Through (1,−2): y=2x−4, so its y-intercept is −4.

questions.question_text: Find the area of the triangle formed by x=0, y=0, and 2x+5y=20.
questions.explanation: Intercepts are (10,0) and (0,4); area=10·4/2=20.

questions.question_text: A point P=(x,y) is equidistant from A(−1,2), B(5,2), and C(2,5). Find P.
questions.explanation: Equidistance from A and B places P on their perpendicular bisector x=2. Equating distances to A and C gives 9+(y−2)²=(y−5)², so 6y=12 and y=2.
